- Vertically integrated fibre-to-fabric manufacturing plus a sustainable paper ecosystem, giving control across the value chain
- Diversified segment mix across bed linen, bath linen, yarn, paper and chemicals, reducing dependence on a single segment
- Captive power plant meeting internal power needs of the business segments
- Global reach — customers in more than 100 countries through enduring partnerships with leading global retailers, brands and institutions
- Presence across both branded and private-label requirements and across retail, hospitality, industrial and export segments
- Scale of workforce and operations — 16,000+ employees
- Presence on 25+ e-commerce websites strengthening direct consumer reach
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Export market concentration — A significant share of revenue remains linked to global demand conditions and trade policies — exports contributed 53.73% of total sale in FY2025-26, so weakness in overseas retail demand or adverse tariff action transmits directly to the top line.
- Geopolitical, tariff and trade disruption — Global conflicts, shipping disruptions and changes in international trade policies may impact exports, supply chains and export competitiveness; management flagged trade barriers, geopolitical developments and supply-chain disruptions across several markets during the year.
- Input cost volatility — Fluctuations in cotton, pulp, fuel chemicals and energy prices can affect margins; freight rate volatility and shipping disruptions can further impact costs and delivery timelines.
- Energy and climate transition risk — Operations in textiles and paper are energy-intensive and dependent on conventional energy sources; failure to mitigate Scope 1, 2 and 3 GHG emissions could expose the Company to carbon pricing mechanisms, carbon taxes and stricter emission reporting obligations, while India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) may raise compliance costs.
- Physical climate risk and cotton raw-material availability — Manufacturing facilities are directly exposed to extreme heat waves, flooding and water scarcity that can disrupt plant operations and damage infrastructure; dependence on cotton as a primary raw material presents supply risk as erratic rainfall, prolonged droughts and rising temperatures drive up procurement costs.
- Capital-intensive and resource-intensive operations — Sustained investments are required for technology upgrades, sustainability initiatives and capacity enhancement, while textile and paper operations consume significant energy, water and raw materials — exposing the Company to both reinvestment burden and evolving environmental compliance costs.
- Intensifying global competition — Competition from low-cost manufacturing nations may exert pricing pressure on Trident's export-facing textile businesses.
- Dependence on skilled workforce and attrition — Large-scale manufacturing operations require continuous availability of skilled and technical talent; the turnover rate for permanent employees was 38.77% in FY2025-26 (40.57% in FY2024-25) and for permanent workers 22.23%.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Trident operates diversified business segments comprising Bed Linen, Bath Linen, Yarn, Paper and Chemicals, supported by a captive power plant that meets the internal power needs of its various business segments. It runs an integrated fibre-to-fabric textile ecosystem alongside a sustainable paper operation that makes high-speed printing and publishing paper, branded copier paper and wheat straw-based paper. The Company serves leading global retailers, brands, hospitality players, institutional buyers, printing and publishing customers and e-commerce platforms across more than 100 countries, in both branded and private-label formats.

outlook.body:
- Fundamental reinvention of the enterprise — investing aggressively in modernisation, automation, digital transformation and Artificial Intelligence to build a globally competitive, technology-led institution
- Premiumisation — increasing the share of design-led and value-added products through high-thread-count bed linen, specialised finishes, differentiated collections and speciality yarns across luxury, fashion accents and sports categories
- Export expansion — deepening presence in the UK under the India-UK Free Trade Agreement through product-mix optimisation, closer customer engagement and programme-based partnerships, and directing greater attention to the Middle East and European markets alongside established North America presence
- Building commercial capability in key international markets through additions to customer-facing teams in the United States, United Kingdom and the GCC region
- Institutionalising innovation via a dedicated Innovation Cell focused on fibres, spinning and weaving technologies, supported by NABL-accredited laboratories and a dedicated team of more than 30 professionals
- Digital Trident agenda — Industry 4.0 adoption with real-time monitoring, smart manufacturing systems and advanced analytics, with AI-driven projects being integrated into operations
- Protecting profitability through cost discipline, operating efficiencies and improving product mix rather than chasing volume
- Strengthening domestic presence and building world-class brands aligned to Viksit Bharat, Atmanirbhar Bharat and the Swadeshi spirit
- Accelerating renewable energy adoption and environmental stewardship, elevating workplace safety and investing in people
- Operating one of India's largest integrated textile manufacturing platforms across yarn, bath linen, bed linen and paper to meet customer requirements for scale, supply assurance, traceability and compliance
- The Company follows a Dividend Distribution Policy that balances the dual objectives of rewarding shareholders through dividends while ensuring the availability of sufficient funds for the growth of the Company, with dividend decisions also taking into account shareholder expectations and past dividend history. In FY2025-26 an interim dividend of Rs 0.50 per share (50% on a face value of Rs 1 each) was declared and paid, and the Board did not recommend a final dividend for the year. No profits were transferred to general reserves and the entire profit for the year forms part of Retained Earnings (apart from a transfer to General Reserve on account of the Employee Stock Option Scheme), and there was no change in share capital during the period. Remuneration to the Non-Executive Independent Director being re-appointed is proposed by way of profit-related commission within the overall limit of 1% of net profits approved by shareholders for Non-Executive Directors, in addition to sitting fees.
- Aspires to become a Net-Zero Company by 2050
- Has set Science Based Targets to reduce Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions
- Has already transitioned over 50% of its energy sourcing to renewables including solar and biomass, significantly reducing dependency on coal
- Expanded captive solar power capacity by 5.40 MWp during FY2025-26, taking total installed captive solar power capacity to 57.38 MWp
- Transitioning from coal-based grid supply to renewable energy sources including solar and IREC-certified renewable energy purchases
- Increasing biofuel consumption and integrating biomass energy to reduce fossil fuel dependency in boiler operations
- Investing in energy-efficient technologies and process optimisations across manufacturing to reduce energy intensity
- Developing robust Scope 1, 2 and 3 GHG inventories and aligning disclosure with TCFD recommendations
- Implementing climate scenario analysis and embedding physical climate risk assessments into infrastructure planning
- Pursuing capex investments in solar and energy-efficient equipment to achieve long-term energy cost reduction
- Seeking to access government schemes such as PAT/CCTS by exceeding energy reduction targets
- Sulphuric acid production at Dhaula, Punjab uses Double Conversion Double Absorption (DCDA) technology aimed at efficient energy utilisation and lower emissions
- Structured double-materiality assessment (impact and financial materiality) covering employees, workers, customers, suppliers, investors, regulators, communities, industry bodies and business partners
- BRSR disclosures obtained Limited Assurance from Intertek India Private Limited
- Enterprise Risk Management framework with a digitised Risk Register, Risk Scores based on likelihood, impact and velocity, named Risk Owners, Chief Risk Officer review and reporting to the Risk Management Committee
- Safety management framework supported by periodic safety trainings, hazard identification and risk assessment, internal audits and structured emergency preparedness programmes across manufacturing locations
- Grievance redressal mechanisms in place for communities, investors, shareholders, employees and workers, customers and value chain partners, with policies published on the Company website
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The only specific expansion disclosed in the routed sections is in the Directors' Report under 'Expansions/Modernisation': during FY2025-26 the Company expanded its captive solar power capacity by 5.40 MWp, taking total installed captive solar power capacity to 57.38 MWp, framed as part of its commitment to reducing its carbon footprint and adopting environmentally responsible energy solutions. There was no change in share capital during the year. Beyond this, expansion intent is stated only qualitatively: the Chairman Emeritus describes a phase of 'fundamental reinvention' involving aggressive investment in modernisation, automation, digital transformation and Artificial Intelligence, expanding capabilities through new technologies, innovative products and new market opportunities, strengthening domestic presence and brand building, and accelerating the commitment to renewable energy; the Corporate Overview lists building future-ready manufacturing capabilities through automation and digitalisation, diversifying into high-value and sustainable product segments, and deepening presence across global markets and the domestic retail/e-commerce ecosystem; and the Managing Director describes accelerated Industry 4.0 adoption with real-time monitoring, smart manufacturing systems and advanced analytics, with AI-driven projects being integrated under the 'Digital Trident' agenda. No plant-level capacity addition project, commissioning timeline, site-wise capex plan or rupee capex outlay is disclosed in these sections.

outlook.body:
- Global brands are placing greater emphasis on scale, supply assurance, traceability and compliance, creating opportunities for integrated manufacturers with established operating capabilities
- Demand in developed markets, particularly the United States, remained subdued for part of the year because of inventory overhang and tariff-related developments; the fourth quarter saw improving order flows driven by inventory replenishment and better retail offtake
- The shift towards premium products continues to reshape the portfolio, improving value realisation, supporting margins and expanding presence across higher-value segments of the global textiles market
- The India-UK Free Trade Agreement provides scope to deepen presence in the UK market
- China-plus-one sourcing by global brands and retailers is expected to strengthen India's and Vietnam's position within global textile supply chains
- Global home textile demand supported by rising consumer spending on home decor, wellness-oriented living spaces, residential housing growth, hospitality refurbishment and organised retail expansion
- Indian home textile demand supported by rising urbanisation, premiumisation, organised retail expansion and higher consumer spending on home decor and lifestyle products
- Regulatory and sustainability shifts — EU Digital Product Passport, traceability and certified sourcing — are driving investment in digital supply-chain infrastructure, recycled fibres and sustainable manufacturing
- Government policy support for textiles — PM MITRA Parks, revised PLI scheme, Kasturi Cotton Bharat, National Technical Textiles Mission, RoSCTL/RoDTEP and Union Budget 2026-27 programmes
- Paper demand supported by education sector demand under the National Education Policy, copier paper consumption from offices and institutions, India's low per capita paper consumption and rising preference for agro-based, recyclable and sustainable paper
- Rising freight, pulp, energy and wastepaper costs exerted pressure on paper industry margins during the year, particularly for import-dependent manufacturers
- Changes in trade patterns, tariff developments in selected markets and shifts in buying patterns across developed economies affected order flows across parts of the textile value chain, particularly in the second half

open.item: The Company is pursuing globally aligned decarbonisation targets and a clear Net Zero 2050 goal, with sustainability embedded into operations and the value chain.
The Company intends to expand its presence across domestic retail and international markets while deepening its consumer ecosystem through retail, e-commerce and strategic partnerships.
The Company intends to diversify into high-value and sustainable product segments and build future-ready manufacturing capabilities through automation and digitalisation.

AI-driven projects are being integrated into operations as part of the broader Digital Trident agenda, following accelerated Industry 4.0 adoption with real-time monitoring, smart manufacturing systems and advanced analytics.

The Company is deepening its UK presence under the India-UK FTA and directing greater attention to the Middle East and European markets, having expanded customer-facing teams in the United States, United Kingdom and the GCC region.

The business is increasing the share of design-led and value-added products — high-thread-count bed linen, specialised finishes, differentiated collections and speciality yarns — to improve value realisation and support margins.

Management flagged that changes in global trade flows, tariff developments in selected markets and inventory overhang in developed markets — particularly the United States — affected order flows across the towel and sheeting businesses.
The Company states it is investing aggressively in modernisation, automation, digital transformation and Artificial Intelligence as part of a fundamental reinvention of the enterprise.
The Company intends to expand its capabilities through new technologies, innovative products and new market opportunities.
The Company states it is accelerating its commitment towards renewable energy and environmental stewardship, elevating workplace safety and investing in its people.
The Company intends to build future-ready manufacturing capabilities through automation and digitalisation and to diversify into high-value and sustainable product segments.
